_comment: Allow-list for scripts/clock-guard.php (I18N-02). A raw MySQL clock function in a string
literal under app/, routes/ or database/ fails CI unless it is listed here with a reason.
The ONLY defensible reason is that the column on the other side of the comparison is
written by the DATABASE (a ->useCurrent() column default), so both sides share the DB
clock. If the column is written by Laravel it is an app-clock value: bind the bound from
PHP (Carbon::today() / now()) as a query parameter instead of reaching for NOW().
See the script's header and docs/DEPLOY-LARAVEL.md for the full reasoning.

allow.reason: Failed-login burst window. Compares audit_log.created_at, which is filled by the column default (timestamp()->useCurrent() in 2026_06_08_120006_create_settings_and_audit) and is therefore a DB-clock value, against the DB clock. Both sides are the same clock, so the 10-minute window is exact whatever the app/DB offset is.

Security panel, last-24h failed-login clusters. Same column and same reasoning as the AuthController entry: audit_log.created_at is DB-written, so comparing it against the DB clock is the correct pairing.
Admin band security-anomaly count; mirrors the Security panel's 24h cluster query exactly (the two numbers must agree) and reads the same DB-written audit_log.created_at.

R2 clock-skew health check: UTC_TIMESTAMP() is read back as a plain value and compared in PHP with Carbon::now('UTC') (both explicit UTC) to measure database-vs-PHP host clock drift for /health. It is never compared against an app-written column, so the session-timezone hazard this guard exists for does not apply.
